title: The Language of Scientific Caution
text:
Scientists rarely state their findings with absolute certainty. Instead, they tend to use hedges such as 'may', 'appears to', and 'it is possible that', which signal that a claim is provisional. Such language is not a sign of weakness; it reflects the discipline's commitment to acknowledging the limits of available evidence.

Hedging also allows writers to take a stance without overcommitting. A researcher who writes 'the results suggest' invites readers to evaluate the claim rather than accept it on authority. Critics, however, argue that excessive hedging can obscure genuinely important conclusions, leaving readers unsure what the author actually believes.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do hedges such as 'may' and 'appears to' signal?
options: That the author is completely certain

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what does the phrase 'the results suggest' invite readers to do?
options: Evaluate the claim rather than accept it on authority
Repeat the findings in a report

questions.text: What does the author imply about hedging in paragraph one?
options: It reflects honesty about the limits of evidence
It shows that the researcher lacks knowledge
It is used only in weak research
It should be avoided in published work

questions.text: What can be inferred from the view of the critics in paragraph two?
options: Too much hedging can make conclusions unclear
Hedging should be removed from all writing

paragraph_translations: Os cientistas raramente apresentam suas descobertas com certeza absoluta. Em vez disso, costumam usar marcadores de cautela, como 'may', 'appears to' e 'it is possible that', que sinalizam que uma afirmação é provisória. Esse tipo de linguagem não é sinal de fraqueza; ele reflete o compromisso da disciplina em reconhecer os limites das evidências disponíveis.

A cautela também permite que os autores assumam uma posição sem se comprometer em excesso. Um pesquisador que escreve 'the results suggest' convida o leitor a avaliar a afirmação, em vez de aceitá-la por autoridade. Os críticos, porém, argumentam que o uso excessivo de cautela pode obscurecer conclusões genuinamente importantes, deixando o leitor sem saber o que o autor realmente acredita.
